function.name: gui_act
function.description: Phone GUI structured action. PREFERRED for any screen operation — no Python needed. Actions: tap/longpress {point or rel, ms?}; swipe {point1+point2 or rel1+rel2, ms}; text {value}; key {value:ENTER}; launch {value:pkg}; back; home; wait {seconds}. COORDINATE UNITS — for each point pass EXACTLY ONE of two spellings, never both: `point` = PIXELS, the same unit dump()/look()/find() report as x/y and obs reports as x/y, so copy them straight through with no arithmetic; `rel` = 0-1000 normalized (top-left origin, x right y down), for ask_vision answers and for targets that are inherently relative. Never convert one into the other yourself and never guess which unit a number is: a pixel pair read as normalized lands hundreds of pixels off with NO error and no hint — you just see diff 0 and re-tap. Passing both, or neither, is rejected with an error naming both options. Pixels outside the current screen are rejected with an error that states the live screen size — resend them as rel. The result carries `obs` — a compact list of what is on screen now ([{t, cls, x, y, rx, ry}], up to 12 items; x/y are pixels usable directly as point, rx/ry are 0-1000 usable directly as rel) — so you can usually pick the next target straight from it instead of spending a separate code_run turn on dump()/look(). Use code_run to observe only when obs is empty or you need something it does not carry. One action per call. Use code_run to OBSERVE the screen (dump()/look()), for multi-step logic, or for non-GUI work — observation is not an action. look/dump are NOT gui_act actions; use code_run for observation. For any search box/search page: tapping the box already raises the IME; do not tap it again to "activate" (a tap on an already-focused box may show diff 0 — not a failure). In sensitive apps (WeChat etc.) text/paste only sets the clipboard; use the visible keyboard paste/clipboard suggestion; if none, long-press the accurately located input-box center using current obs/screen coordinates, then tap the paste menu. A long-press on blank space can dismiss the keyboard/search box; do not repeat paste. Icon-only title/toolbar buttons (magnifier, +, back, menu): locate them in TWO tiers, never guess. ① `look(roi='title')` in code_run — when an Android UI detector model is installed it also returns `type='icon'` boxes (cls is the widget semantics, x/y are full-screen pixels you can pass straight to `point`). Measured on this device: one look() returns the WeChat magnifier at (997,216) and + at (1117,214) in 31ms. ② Only if look() gives no icon box, `droid.ask_point(<what to find>, roi='title')` in code_run — it asks the current model for a 0-1000 pair with a fixed prompt and rejects percent answers — then pass the returned pair to `rel` unchanged and verify after tapping. Never derive an icon position from status-bar time/battery text, and never write your own ask_vision coordinate question (that drifted once into "percentage(0-100)", the VLM answered in prose, and the tap hit the status bar).

point.description: [x,y] in PIXELS — same unit as dump()/look()/obs x/y; copy straight through

value.description: content to type (text), package name (launch), or IME key name (key); never a coordinate

rel.description: [x,y] in 0-1000 normalized (top-left origin) — ask_vision answers, relative targets

function.name: code_run
function.description: Code executor. Prefer python (in-process exec). ALWAYS pass code in the 'script' arg. The reply code block is only a fallback when script is absent (must be a ```python-tagged block), and this tool call must still be made — replying with code without calling this tool executes nothing (the turn is wasted). No hardcoding bulk data The 'script' is plain Python: do not include </script> or other HTML tags; they cause SyntaxError.

script.description: [Mutually exclusive] NEVER use this param when use reply code block.

inline_eval.description: DO NOT USE except explicitly specified.

function.name: file_read
function.description: Read file. Read before modify for latest context and line numbers

keyword.description: [Optional] If provided, returns first match (case-insensitive) with context

function.name: file_patch
function.description: Replace unique old_content with new_content. Exact match required (whitespace/indentation). On failure, file_read to recheck

old_content.description: Original text block to replace (must be unique)

new_content.description: New content. Supports {{file:path:startLine:endLine}} to ref file lines, auto-expanded

function.name: file_write
function.description: Create/overwrite/append files. HUGE edits ONLY. Supports {{file:path:startLine:endLine}}, auto-expanded

function.name: update_working_checkpoint
function.description:
Short-term working notepad, auto-injected each turn to prevent info loss in long tasks. Call during early/mid stages, not at end. When: (1) after reading SOP, store user needs & key constraints (skip for simple 1-2 step tasks); (2) before subtask switch or context flush; (3) after repeated failures, re-read SOP and must store new findings; (4) on new task, update content, clear old progress but keep valid constraints.

Don't call: simple tasks (1-2 steps), task completed (use long-term memory tool)

key_info.description: Replaces current notepad (<200 tokens). Incremental update: review existing, keep valid, add/remove/modify. Store: pitfalls, user requirements, key params/findings, file paths, progress, next steps. Don't store: ephemeral info, obvious context, old task info when user switched tasks. Prefer over-updating over losing key info

related_sop.description: Related SOP names, tips for further re-read

function.name: ask_user
function.description: Interrupt task to ask user when needing decisions, extra info, or facing unresolvable blockers

candidates.description: Optional quick-select choices for the user

function.name: start_long_term_update
function.description: Start distilling long-term memory. Call when discovering info worth remembering (env facts/user prefs/lessons learned). Skip if memory already updated or in autonomous flow. Must call when a task that took 15+ turns is completed
